abstract.gco:CharacterString: STATcube – Statistical Database of STATISTICS AUSTRIA Subject of the statistics Studies at public universities starting from winter semester 2003/04. .) Legal basis Bildungsdokumentationsgesetz, Bundesstatistikgesetz 2000, Universitäts- und Hochschulstatistik- und Bildungsdokumentationsverordnung – UHSBV .) Updating, periodicity New data are stored twice a year. New winter term data are available in the end of each August at the latest, new summer term data in the end of March of the following year. .) Documentation Directorate Social Statistics – Labour Market and Education University Statistics Team Tel.: +43 1 711 28-7349 E-Mail: hochschulstatistik@statistik.gv.at Other Metadata: https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/education/university-students-studies From winter semester 2016/17 the studies are counted according § 22 UHSBV. This means that studies have to be rounded to whole numbers and there may be discrepancies between the total and the added detailed results. In the surveys based on the Ordinance on University and Higher Education Statistics and Educational Documentation - UHSBV, Federal Law Gazette II No. 216/2019, gender is also surveyed for diverse and all other gender that are neither male nor female (third sex). Due to the small number of cases of persons with the third sex, they are assigned to the binary forms male or female by imputation for data protection reasons in STATcube. DescriptionStatistics Austria provides data each semester about students and courses of studies taken at Austrian higher education institutions (public and private universities, theological schools, universities of applied sciences and university colleges of teacher education) as well as data about the origin of students and their parents educational attainment. The legal basis is provided by the Federal Act on Documentation in Education (Bildungsdokumentationsgesetz 2020) and the Regulation on the Statistics of Universities and Higher Education Institutions and on Education Documentation (UHSBV). The main sources of data are the registers of the higher education institutions and data from the primary statistical survey at the beginning of studies (UHStat1). The key figures are the number of students and courses of studies taken at Austrian higher education institutions. purpose.gco:CharacterString:
Austrian universities that have STEM-related fields of study are shown here. The data includes field of study, university, sex and semester. This service aims to visualize the locations of the universities and will be utilized in a streamlit dashboard that visualizes the differences in genders in STEM related fields of study.
STEM stands for science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Whereas, this is a much needed field for the development of todays society, there is still a significant gender gap worldwide. On average girls are four times less likely to pursue career in STEM, which is not least due to mental barriers and lack of personal examples. “Research suggests that exposing girls to female inventors at a young age has the potential to reduce the gender gap in technical STEM fields by half. „ Unfortunately the chance of a young girls interacting with women in STEM is much higher in some universities compared to others. By exploring the spatial aspect of STEM-related education in public universities in Austria we will help detect areas experiencing gender gap and thus of need for awareness raising initiatives.
